track: NeurIPS 2026 AI for Chip Design workshop, POSTER (<=4pp body EXCL refs, non-archival)
title: VerifyNext: Co-Evolving Testbench/Property Generator and Formal Verifier for RTL under Fixed Verification Budget
pivot_rationale: Pivoted from O01 GuardedFlow (Handbook rank #1, Crosswalk fit 29/30) to O02 VerifyNext (rank #2, fit 28/30) on 2026-08-16 after OpenROAD-flow-scripts Docker image failed at CTS stage under Rosetta 2 with 'illegal instruction' — a hard ISA-translation limit, not a speed issue. OpenLane fallback also required PDK+design-corpus port. Native macOS ARM64 OpenROAD binary does not exist (no brew formula, no prebuilt release). OSS CAD Suite provides a complete native ARM64 formal-verification stack (yosys + sby + z3 + cvc5 + boolector + bitwuzla + yices + AIG tools + verilator) that fully satisfies O02's compute requirements. This pivot exchanges ~1 Crosswalk fit point for a 100% working local toolchain and zero Docker/Rosetta dependency.
hypothesis_statement: In LLM-driven RTL verification, generators trained end-to-end against their own preference distribution silently lose ground on hidden mutants and missed properties as they improve. VerifyNext places the generator inside a co-evolving loop where an allocator distributes a fixed verification budget across simulation and bounded formal proof, and where surviving mutants + missed properties become the next curriculum — while an independently-authored anchor stays OUTSIDE the generator's optimization channel. Primary estimand: hidden-mutation-detection per unit verification cost (simulation-seconds + SMT-solver-seconds + LLM-token-cost) at matched budget, co-evolve vs strongest deterministic-allocator baseline.
hero_mechanism: co-evolution loop (generator ↔ allocator) with independent-anchor separation

E3 audit unchanged (E3 does not exercise the deterministic-allocator on sequential separately). Scalar cost function unchanged. Kill rules (KR-1, KR-2, KR-3) unchanged.
freeze_amendment_log.cohort_relationship_to_prior_amendments: Independent of amendments 2-4 (backend, corpus, sequential extension). freeze_amendment_5 is a KR-1 protocol correction, not a corpus/generator change. Applies to the 3 sequential designs added in amendment_4 which exposed the R34 gap when their KR-1 fallback zero-killed.
freeze_amendment_log.why_not_variant_shopping: This amendment STRENGTHENS the deterministic baseline, which WEAKENS the LLM co-evolve loop's relative position — the SAME direction as the pre-registered fallback A adoption (which already reports co-evolve losing). A variant-shopper would have WEAKENED the baseline further to make co-evolve look better; we go the opposite direction. The paper's central negative-result claim becomes STRONGER after the amendment, and the honest observable-mutant reporting shifts from 'co-evolve out-covers KR-1 by +27pp' (pre-amendment) to 'co-evolve is out-covered by KR-1 by 31pp' (post-amendment) — a deliberate concession to a stronger baseline, not a rescue of the co-evolve story.
freeze_amendment_log.corrective_action_for_next_paper: Add a build.sh gate that flags any KR-1 baseline whose per-design kill-rate is 0 on more than 20% of designs — such a baseline is likely broken by R34 and should either use a stronger technique (formal miter, spec-driven inline template) or be excluded from the paired comparison with a documented reason. Hermes rule r34_sequential_template_risk.md documents the pre-flight checks.
freeze_amendment_log.authority: session's autonomous decision under the maintainer's 2026-08-22 mandate 'do the necessary (a), and check all the hermes profile papers tools and knowledge for tips for improving it'; supported by hermes lesson chipdesign_o02_verifynext_execution_lessons R34 (the original spec-violation flag) + r34_sequential_template_risk.md (the safer-path recommendation banked earlier this session).

freeze_amendment_log.amended_at_pass: R5 acceptance-maximization pass. Two changes. (1) E2 PILOT SUBSET: pre-declared 36-cell slice of the pre-registered 360-cell E2 (12 VerilogEval designs x 1 seed x 3 pre-registered systems x 1 backend=agy hosted-model (name redacted)); deterministic family-keyword selection rule + mechanical screen written into CHANGELOG_v3.md BEFORE the run; second LLM backend never provisioned, so the LLM-swap-invariance falsifier half stays untested and full E2 remains planned. (2) KR-1 ON VERILOGEVAL: tops are anonymised (RefModule), no spec-derived arithmetic template is well-defined, so per the freeze_amendment_5 definition (per-design-class strongest deterministic technique) KR-1 routes VerilogEval designs to the bounded z3/depth-2 miter instead of the no-golden always-PASS fallback.
freeze_amendment_log.why_not_variant_shopping: Change (2) STRENGTHENS the deterministic baseline the LLM systems must beat on the transfer slice (the no-golden fallback would have given co-evolve a free win against a 0-kill strawman). Change (1) commits to reporting the pilot whichever way it comes out, with the transfer-score falsifier (TS<=1 fires) applied as pre-registered; a shopping-style amendment would have picked designs after seeing results or weakened the baseline. Both changes move in the direction that makes the paper's LLM-negative story HARDER to sustain, not easier.
